newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest runoff forecasts rise slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest runoff forecasts rise slightly.

text.p: The Northwest River Forecast Center's latest update of spring runoff forecasts for hydroelectric projects in the Pacific Northwest calls for levels slightly higher than the previous update.

In its "early-bird" March assessment, the center forecast January to July runoff on the Columbia River at The Dalles dam in Oregon at 133 percent of average, compared with a mid-February estimate of 132 percent.
Last year runoff at The Dalles during the same period was 132 percent of average, near 140 million acre feet (maf).

April to July inflow to the Brownlee reservoir on the Snake River in Idaho was forecast at a revised 105 maf or 181 percent of average rates, compared with the mid-February forecast of 174 percent of average.
The January-July inflow forecast for the Lower Granite reservoir on the Snake in Washington was increased to 159 percent of average from 153 percent in mid-February.
